explain.say: Have you ever wondered who pays for your school desk or the streetlights outside? In a way, you do, along with all the grown-ups around you. Look at the board: a circle showing how tax money travels and comes back to you.

explain.say: See pay taxes light up? A tax is money people and businesses must pay to the government. Some comes from wages, and some is added to prices, like India's GST, Nigeria's VAT or Japan's consumption tax. Have you seen tax on a shop receipt?

explain.say: Next, the government budget, which is a plan for spending. Every year leaders decide how much goes to schools, health, roads and defence, and parliament votes on it. If you were in charge, what would get the most?

faq.a: A tax is money that people and businesses must pay to the government. It can be taken from wages, added to the price of things you buy, or charged on property and profits.

faq.q: Who decides how taxes are spent?
faq.a: The government plans a yearly budget, and the parliament or congress debates and votes on it. Local councils decide how to spend local taxes.
Schools, hospitals, roads, police, fire crews, clean water, pensions for older people, and defence. Each country chooses its own mix.
Children usually do not pay income tax. But when you buy a snack, part of the price is often a sales tax like GST or VAT, so yes, you pay a little!

faq.q: What happens if people do not pay taxes?
faq.a: They can be fined or taken to court. And when people avoid tax, there is less money for services, and others who pay their share end up carrying more.
asks: Is it illegal not to pay tax?
